newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli retail sales rose 12 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Israeli retail sales rose 12 percent in 1996.

text.p: Sales at Israeli retail chain stores rose 12 percent after inflation in 1996, but growth fell sharply after the first quarter of the year, the Central Bureau of Statistics said on Tuesday.
The bureau said retail sales rose at an 18 percent annualised rate in the first quarter but that growth fell in the next three quarters to a six to nine percent rate.
The bureau did not provide shekel figures.

Supermarket sales outpaced other segments, rising 16 percent for the year. In the first quarter supermarket sales rose an annualised 18 percent, like other retail segments, but growth only fell to a 13 to 14 percent pace in the following three quarters.
The survey includes sales of textiles and clothing, shoes, consumer durables, but not automobiles or energy products.
The bureau said sales of textiles, clothing and shoes rose only nine percent while sales of consumer durables were almost unchanged.
